bounded_proposition: Around 1400 the Swahili maritime network participated in a persistent but comparatively modest medieval slave trade, with concrete node-level slavery evidence at Kilwa and bounded fifteenth-century archaeological evidence at Songo Mnara. Network participation is supported; coast-wide territorial practice, uniformity and scale remain unresolved.
required_abstention: Do not infer one Swahili polity or uniform coast-wide practice; do not infer slave trading from maritime connectivity alone; do not generalize Kilwa or Songo Mnara to every node; do not project nineteenth-century Zanzibar plantation scale backward; do not convert source counts into prevalence or trade volume.
evidence_locus: Kilwa 1331; Rasulid/Yemeni maritime-customs context for thirteenth/fourteenth-century East Africa-Arabia trade; Songo Mnara fifteenth century; Tumbatu/Mkokotoni c.1000-1400; specialist Swahili-coast synthesis
inference_extent: Positive network-level slave-trade participation around the anchor plus bounded node-level local slavery/practice; territorial prevalence, participation by every port and exact network volume withheld.
law_practice_note: No single coast-wide legal regime is assigned; Islamic legal/social context is relevant but not used to infer uniform local law. Practice and network participation rest on bounded primary/site evidence plus specialist synthesis.
network_territorial_note: External/network slave-trade participation is supported. Local territorial slavery is supported only at bounded nodes; network membership does not transfer territorial practice to all ports or coastlands.
historical_terms: slave; enslaved person; captive; raid; client; dependent; domestic worker; migrant; maritime trade
category_mapping_note: Slave trading, local slaveholding, raiding, clientship, migration and other dependency remain distinct; archaeological low-status proxies are not automatic slave-status proof.
language_access_limitations: English specialist scholarship and translated Ibn Battuta reviewed; no exhaustive Arabic, Portuguese, Swahili or Rasulid archival corpus and no source-native customs edition reconstructed in this pass.
geometry_unresolved_note: No route line or Swahili-coast polygon is promoted to slavery-practice geometry; Kilwa, Songo Mnara and Tumbatu/Mkokotoni remain bounded evidence/navigation loci.
